extracted.intended_audience: applicants and practitioners filing international design (Hague System) applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and filing international design applications under the WIPO Hague System (including eHague and paper form DM/1), covering reproductions, multiple designs, technical image requirements, languages and fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing method: eHague recommended
rubrics_metrics.description: The simplest way to file your international design applications is using eHague – our secure, intuitive and real-time online platform. You may also file an application using Hague System form DM/1. However, we strongly recommend that you file online using eHague.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advantages of eHague: complete digital access to all aspects of your application (save, view, download, check processing status, reply to communications from WIPO, and easily pay online). eHague handles forms, supporting documents and cost calculations for you. New users can follow the eHague filing tutorial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility check before filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Want to file an international application? First check your eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the eligibility check resources provided by WIPO before starting an application to ensure you can use the Hague System for your design(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Languages permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: You can file your application in English, French or Spanish – the official languages of the Hague System.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all parts of the filing conform to one of the Hague System official languages to avoid processing issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number and classification of designs per application
rubrics_metrics.description: Your application can include up to 100 designs (within the same class of the Locarno Classification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All designs in a single international application must fall in the same Locarno class. If designs belong to different classes, file separate applications. Use the Guide to the Hague System and Member Profiles to confirm classification and national requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproductions required for each design
rubrics_metrics.description: You must include a reproduction of each design covered. One design may be represented by many reproductions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide all specific views required to disclose the design fully. Guidance on reproductions explains how to avoid unnecessary refusals on the grounds of insufficient disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproduction background and description requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Reproductions must be on a neutral, plain background. (If you need to use color background, you must refer to this in the description.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a non-neutral or colored background is used, explicitly state this in the design description. Failure to follow background and description guidance can lead to objections or refusals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency and disclaimers for reproductions
rubrics_metrics.description: Reproductions must be consistent and correspond to each other. Only textual or graphical disclaimers are accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all images of the same design match in representation (no conflicting views). Do not include non-accepted disclaimers; stick to textual or graphical disclaimers only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical image requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide all images at 300 dpi. Keep a minimum of one pixel of border (maximum 20 pixels) to allow for cropping, pre-publication. Maximum file size is 2MB. Maximum 1890 x 1890 pixels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow all technical requirements (resolution, border, file size, dimensions) to avoid upload problems, cropping that obscures the design, or pre-publication issues. See the full technical requirements page for additional format and file-type details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees: payment of required fees and fee estimation
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications are subject to the payment of three types of fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Hague System fee calculator to quickly estimate your application or renewal fees. Ensure payment of the required fees at filing to avoid delays or refusals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple designs: unity and national treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: You can include up to 100 designs in one international application so long as they fall in the same class of the Locarno Classification. The domestic legal framework of each Hague System Contracting Party governs the design protection provided by an international registration. Some Contracting Parties require unity of design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your designs do not meet pre-defined domestic requirements (e.g., unity of design), individual Contracting Parties can refuse the effects of your international registration within their territory pending compliance. A refusal in one Contracting Party does not affect your international registration in other designated jurisdictions. Consult Member Profiles and Declarations to anticipate national requirements and avoid processing delays; download WIPO guidance on multiple designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk of insufficient disclosure and required views
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure you provide all specific views. Guidance on reproductions helps avoid unnecessary refusals on the grounds of insufficient disclosure of your designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include multiple reproductions showing all aspects of the design (e.g., front, back, sides, perspective) as needed by national practices. Failure to provide sufficient views can cause a refusal or require correction in some designated Contracting Parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic declarations and member-specific rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Declarations made by Contracting Parties may impact on your international applications and registrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the Hague System Member Profiles and the Hague legal texts (Hague Administrative Instructions, Part Four; Hague Common Regulations, Rule 9) to understand member-specific requirements, declarations and how they affect processing and protection.
